error_events.evidence: Answers the planner's 'check ... for any duplicate flights on the same day' with intra-itinerary connections instead of duplicate bookings: reports "Reservation 'HTR26G': Flights on 2024-05-16 (MSP-EWR-DFW) are on the same day" although the get_reservation_details result shows HTR26G is a single one-way MSP->DFW booking whose two legs are one connection, and states "Reservation '5BGGWZ': Flights on 2024-05-10 (EWR-DFW) and 2024-05-17 (DFW-EWR) are not on the same day" although 5BGGWZ's 2024-05-17 DFW->EWR leg collides with SE9KEL and FDZ0T5 on 2024-05-17. The duplicate set the customer is asked to choose from at step 10 is therefore wrong (real cross-reservation collisions: 2024-05-17 SE9KEL/FDZ0T5/5BGGWZ and 2024-05-22 PUNERT/HSR97W).

Delegates "Check if the cancellation of Reservation 'FDZ0T5' is allowed under the airline's policy" with none of the facts needed to apply the policy, although the db_agent had already returned FDZ0T5's record at step 6 (cabin business, created_at 2024-05-13T08:25:23, insurance no). policy_checker can only answer 'VERDICT: need_info' (steps 14-15), burning three steps. Recovered at step 19, where the planner re-asks with booking date, cabin class and insurance.

The planner's final turn is the literal text '<tool_call>\n{"name": "respond_to_user", "arguments": {...}}\n</tool_call>' emitted as message content with no tool call at all (finish_reason=stop, tool_calls=[]), although respond_to_user was in its tool list; the episode ends there. The 2024-05-22 duplicate pair PUNERT/HSR97W that the db_agent had reported at step 7 is never cancelled, although the customer said at step 11 'Could you handle the rest for the other days as well?' and the task requires one cancellation per duplicated day (user is in BOS on May 22, so HSR97W should have gone). reward 0.0.
